description: Unique USGS event identifier.
Origin time of the event in UTC (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
Origin date (UTC).
Origin year.
Origin month (1-12).
Origin day of month.
Origin hour (0-23, UTC).
Day of week of the origin time.
Timestamp of the most recent revision of the event record.
Human-readable location description.
Last component of the place string, usually the country or region.
Epicentre latitude in decimal degrees.
Epicentre longitude in decimal degrees.
Hypocentre depth in kilometres below sea level.
Depth band: shallow (<70 km), intermediate (<300 km), deep.
Preferred magnitude.
Magnitude scale used (ml, mb, mww, md, ...).
Descriptive band: minor, light, moderate, strong, major, great.
Number of seismic stations used in the location solution.
Largest azimuthal gap between stations, in degrees (lower is better).
Distance to the nearest station in degrees.
Root-mean-square travel-time residual of the location, in seconds.
Contributing seismic network code (e.g. us, ak, ci).
Event type: earthquake, quarry blast, explosion, ice quake, ...
Review status of the solution: reviewed or automatic.
1 if the event is in a region where a tsunami could be generated.
Number of DYFI 'felt it' reports received.
Maximum Community Decimal Intensity from felt reports.
Maximum estimated Modified Mercalli Intensity.
PAGER alert level: green, yellow, orange or red.
USGS significance score combining magnitude, felt reports and impact.
Number of contributing data sources.
Semicolon-separated contributing source codes.
USGS event page URL.
